title: Adaptive gradient microbatching and kernel hinting to reduce embedding tail latency
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Goal: reduce p95/p99 latency for the embedding endpoint while preserving throughput and embedding quality. We will implement an adaptive microbatching controller that adjusts microbatch sizes on-the-fly using a throughput-gradient signal, add lightweight kernel hinting metadata to the request router so the runtime can pick faster kernels for common sequence-length/precision pairs, and pre-warm KV cache paths for repeated embed prefixes. The ticket focuses on profiling, a small runtime change, and a gradual rollout with feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 for 512-token embedding requests reduced by >= 30% on staging under representative traffic mix
No regression in cosine similarity for validation prompt set (delta < 0.002 per-pair)
Adaptive controller respects latency SLOs and does not reduce overall throughput by > 10% at peak
Feature gated behind 'adaptive-embed-microbatch' and 'kernel-hinting' flags and has observability dashboards
comments: 2026-03-01 - Miguel Santos: Initial write-up and proposal. Hypothesis: static microbatch sizes cause tail spikes when request-size distribution shifts. Proposed solution: a short-window gradient estimator adjusts microbatch target between 1..8 requests and signals preferred kernel via router hints.

2026-03-03 - Ava Patel: Added kernel-hinting design after spike profiling. Suggests a hint enum (FAST_32F_SHORT, FAST_8BIT_LONG, BALANCED) instead of raw capex parameters to keep router/runtime contract small.
2026-03-04 - Dev Ops (review): Noted that pre-warming KV cache may increase memory churn on high-cardinality prefixes. Recommendation: limit pre-warm to top-N prefixes per model and an LRU throttle.

2026-03-06 - Miguel: Ran microbench harness with synthetic traffic representing 60% short (64 tokens), 30% mid (256 tokens), 10% long (1024 tokens). Baseline p99=320ms, after adaptive controller p99=210ms (~34% improvement). Detailed heatmap uploaded.
2026-03-07 - Design review (Jamie Liu): Reviewed fallbacks and UX for console flags. Request to surface per-model artifact advising when to disable adaptive batching for small enterprise latencies.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/7642 - includes adaptive controller, kernel hint enum, and added metrics (microbatch_target, hint_chosen, hitch_count).
2026-03-10 - QA: Started canary on staging with 10% traffic. Observed 15% throughput loss on one worker type due to aggressive pre-warm; lowered pre-warm N from 50 to 12 and re-ran canary.

2026-03-12 - Miguel: Updated controller to include cost-aware penalty term so it prefers smaller microbatches when worker GPU utilization > 78% to avoid throughput cliffs. Also added unit test for hint->kernel mapping.

2026-03-12 - Link to artifacts: Design doc https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aB-embed-design, Perf heatmap https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/heatmap, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7642
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adaptive microbatching can reduce packing efficiency and increase per-token cost if traffic shifts to many very small requests; mitigations include cost-aware penalty and conservative escalation windows
Kernel hinting adds a tight contract between router and runtime; we limit the enum to 4 entries to preserve forward compatibility
KV pre-warm improves tail for repeated prefixes but increases memory usage; we will cap pre-warms per-worker and measure resident set size impact
